verdict.rationale: Algolia's docs say it provides typo tolerance out of the box, "along with some important ways to customize just how tolerant a search experience should be" [algolia-docs-7, algolia-docs-45], and treat typos as a core relevance factor [algolia-docs-66]. Independent users credit its typo handling in real deployments [algolia-comm-16, algolia-comm-18]. One HN user wishing fuzzy matching could be turned off is a feature wish about one deployment, not a concrete contradiction of the documented tuning. Missing for 10: specific documentation of the tuning controls (e.g., word-length thresholds, per-attribute or per-query disabling of typo tolerance), and hands-on evidence that those controls work as described.
